input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: Section 2.2 (the first of two provisions numbered 2.2) binds us to Copperleaf as sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the entire term, with no category limitation, no 12-month cap and no performance-based exit. That is exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance exit, i.e. walk-away territory and a clear failure of the fallback. The exclusivity runs against us (not in our favour), and it also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment. Redline moves to the preferred position by making supply non-exclusive and confirming our freedom to source from third parties; a narrowed 12-month category exclusivity with automatic termination on missed service levels remains available as a fallback if commercially required.

ops.oldText: Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
ops.newText: Vendor will be a non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services, and Customer may procure the same or similar services from any third party at any time.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the sole-and-exclusive supplier commitment so that we remain free to source hosted analytics services elsewhere, consistent with our playbook position against exclusivity binding the customer. If exclusivity matters commercially, we could discuss a narrow category-specific arrangement capped at 12 months that ends automatically if service levels or delivery dates are missed.
proposal.summary: Convert Vendor's sole and exclusive provider status to non-exclusive supply.
